products.name: Neo4j
products.description: Leading native graph database platform with property graph model, Cypher query language, cloud (AuraDB) and enterprise options. Market leader with 80+ Fortune 100 customers, GraphRAG positioning, and knowledge layer for AI systems.
products.positioning: Enterprise-grade knowledge graph platform for OLTP and analytical workloads, positioned as foundation for AI/GraphRAG systems

products.name: TigerGraph
products.description: Massively parallel processing (MPP) graph database engineered for analytics and deep-link queries. GSQL query language compiles to C++ binaries. Optimized for billion-edge scale, real-time streaming, and 10+ hop traversals with aggressive compression.
products.positioning: Enterprise graph analytics platform for distributed deep-link queries and real-time insights at scale

products.name: Memgraph
products.description: Open-source in-memory graph database with Cypher compatibility (Neo4j migration path). Built for streaming and real-time analytics. Positioned for AI memory systems. Early-stage funding (seed), used by enterprises like NASA and Cedars-Sinai.
products.positioning: High-performance in-memory graph database for real-time streaming analytics and AI memory systems

products.name: ArangoDB
products.description: Multi-model database unifying graph, document, key-value, vector, and full-text search via single AQL query language. Rebranding to 'Arango' with Contextual Data Platform and Agentic AI Suite. Positioned for GraphRAG and graph-based AI systems.
products.positioning: Multi-model data platform for graph, document, and AI workloads with unified query language (AQL)

products.name: Kuzu
products.description: Embedded graph database for analytical queries, optimized for complex join-heavy workloads on large graphs. MIT licensed, columnar disk-based storage, vectorized query processing. Acquired by Apple (Oct 2025) and archived; community fork (LadybugDB) continues development.
products.positioning: Lightweight embedded graph database for analytical workloads; legacy project (archived post-Apple acquisition)

products.name: FalkorDB
products.description: Graph database optimized for GraphRAG and agentic AI, built as Redis module using sparse adjacency matrices (GraphBLAS). Sub-millisecond latency, multi-tenant support, linear scalability. Emerging competitor targeting AI/GenAI use cases.
products.positioning: Latency-optimized graph database for GraphRAG and agentic AI systems, leveraging sparse matrix design

notes: Market landscape notes: (1) Neo4j dominates OLTP/knowledge graphs; TigerGraph dominates OLAP/analytics; Memgraph leads in-memory/streaming; ArangoDB leads multi-model; FalkorDB leads low-latency/GraphRAG. (2) GraphRAG emergence (2026) is shaping all competitive positioning — from Neo4j's acquisition of GraphAware (June 2026) to FalkorDB's SDK launch to ArangoDB's AutoGraph. (3) Kuzu's Apple acquisition (Oct 2025) removes it from competition; community fork (LadybugDB) continues but not production-ready. (4) All platforms support Cypher or GQL-compatible languages; no clear query-language winner (industry converging on GQL standard ISO/IEC 39075:2024). (5) HCI/visualization pain points documented across all platforms (MIT Lincoln Lab research on LLM-assisted KG exploration; 15 Neo4j visualization tools; no unified interface). (6) Key wedge opportunities for MetroGraph: reduce surface area from 30+ visualization/workflow tools to unified metro-map canvas; fix learning curve (GSQL vs Cypher vs AQL); enable natural language graph building; integrate workflow orchestration for data engineers.
